newsitem.title: TURKEY: FORECAST-Turkey 8-mo trade deficit seen at $11 bln.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Turkey 8-mo trade deficit seen at $11 bln.

text.p: Turkey's January-August trade deficit is estimated to have risen to around $11 billion, sharply up from $8 billion in the same 1995 period, state minister Ayfer Yilmaz said on Monday.

According to provisional customs figures, exports stood at around $16 billion and imports at $27 billion in the first eight months of this year, Yilmaz was quoted as saying by the Anatolian news agency.
Yilmaz said the figures were provisional and might change by about five percent. Exports were $13.9 billion and imports $21.5 billion in January-August 1995.

Turkey's trade deficit was $2.4 billion at the end of February, according to offical data which has been delayed due to technical problems arising from Turkey's customs union with the European Union this year.
Yilmaz, in charge of foreign trade, had recently said Turkey's 1996 trade deficit would stand at around $20 billion, against a government target of $16 billion.
